items.title: Immeasurable Strength, Effortless Skill, Awakening Without a Teacher, and Brahmā's Own Request

items.zh: 於稚童時，不由習學，自然善巧，於諸世間工巧業處疾疾能入。無師自然獨處三千大千世界，證得無上正等菩提。
items.en: In childhood, without any training at all, they are naturally skilful, swiftly mastering every worldly craft. Without a teacher, dwelling alone in the great trichiliocosm, they attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

items.zh: 索訶界主大梵天王自然來下，慇懃勸請哀愍世間宣說正法。
items.en: Great Brahmā, lord of this Sahā world-system, comes down of his own accord, earnestly beseeching the Buddha, out of compassion for the world, to expound the true teaching.

items.title: Section: Unshakeable Meditation — The Woman in Samādhi Only One Bodhisattva Could Wake

items.zh: 其定寂靜，設大雲雷，曾無覺受，安然不起。
items.en: Their concentration is so utterly still that, even should great thunderclouds roll in, they experience no disturbance whatsoever, remaining perfectly at peace.

items.zh: 為菩薩時，一切禽獸蠕動之類，皆極仰信，常來歸趣，隨其所欲親附而住。既成佛已，下至傍生亦來供養。如彼獼猴獻清淨蜜，世尊哀受，歡喜舞躍。龍雲常候，洗便降雨；若出遊行，止而不落。菩薩如是若坐樹下，一切枝條並皆垂影，隨蔭其身，曾無虧捨。

items.title: Perfect Stillness in Rest, Effortless Grace in Walking, and Food That Never Fails to Nourish

items.zh: 證菩提已，於六年中，魔求其便竟不能得。常俱行念每恒現前；由此念故，受想尋思生住滅等無不覺了。又佛成就俱生威力，或有見便饒益所攝，或有賢聖行住所攝。見便饒益所攝俱生威力者，謂諸世間若見如來，癲癎心亂還得本心，逆胎得順，盲者得視，聾者能聽，懷貪欲者得離貪纏，懷瞋恚者得離瞋纏，懷愚癡者得離癡纏。如是
items.en: Having attained awakening, for six full years Māra sought any opening at all and never once found one. Constant mindfulness remains always present; through this mindfulness, feeling and perception, discursive thought, and the arising, abiding, and ceasing of bodily movement and the rest — all of body, speech, and mind — are without exception fully known. ... Whenever the bodhisattva sits beneath a tree, every branch bends to cast its shade over his body, never once failing to shelter him.

items.zh: 等類，當知是名見便饒益所攝俱生威力。
賢聖行住所攝俱生威力者，謂佛菩薩常右脇臥，如師子王。雖現安處草葉等蓐，一脇而臥，曾無動亂。一切如來應正等覺，雖現睡眠而無轉側。大風卒起，不動身衣。行如師子，步若牛王。先舉右足，方移左足。隨所行地，高處便下，下處遂高，坦然如掌，無諸礫石、塼瓦等物。心專遠離而入聚落，隨所入門，門若狹小自然高廣。食所食時，有粒皆碎，無口不殫。
items.en: The innate power belonging to noble conduct in rest and motion: buddhas and bodhisattvas always sleep lying on their right side, like a lion king ... every Tathāgata, though appearing to sleep, never shifts position. Even a sudden strong wind does not stir their body or robes. Their walk is like a lion's, their stride like a bull-king's. ... When eating, every grain of food is thoroughly broken down; not a single mouthful goes undigested.

items.zh: 如是等類，當知是名賢聖行住所攝俱生威力。

items.title: Section: The Marks of Final Nirvāṇa Close Innate Power in Full

items.zh: 般涅槃時，大地振動，眾星晃耀，交流而隕，諸方一時欻然大熱，遍滿虛空奏天大樂。
items.en: At the time of final nirvāṇa, the great earth quakes, the stars shine and stream across the sky before falling, every direction suddenly grows intensely hot all at once, and heavenly music resounds throughout the whole of space.

items.zh: 如是無量甚希有事，皆是如來俱生威力，非是神通威力所作。如是名為諸佛菩薩俱生威力。
items.en: All such immeasurable and truly extraordinary events as these are the Tathāgata's own innate power, not something produced by deliberately exercised miraculous ability. This is called the innate power of buddhas and bodhisattvas.

items.zh: 云何諸佛菩薩威力，與聲聞、獨覺有共不共？略由三相應知不共。一者、微細故；二者、品類故；三者、界故。諸佛菩薩於無量無數諸有情類，及無量無數威力方便，如所應作諸利益事，皆如實知，無不能作。是名微細。

items.title: Section: What Sets Buddhas Apart — Complete Mastery, and a Scope Reaching Every World and Every Being

items.zh: 一切品類神通威力、法威力、俱生威力悉皆成就。是名品類。以一切世界、一切有情界為威力境。是名為界。聲聞但以二千世界及有情界為神通境，獨覺但以三千世界為神通境。
items.en: Every kind of miraculous power, power of the Dharma, and innate power is completely accomplished. This is called their kind. Every world-system and every realm of sentient beings serves as the domain of their power. This is called their scope. Hearers take only a two-thousand-fold world-system, together with the beings in it, as the domain of their miraculous ability; solitary buddhas take only a three-thousand-fold world-system as that domain.

items.zh: 何以故？由彼唯為調伏一身而修正行，非諸有情；是故最極唯以一界為神通境。
items.en: Why is this? Because a solitary buddha cultivates their practice only to tame their own single existence, not for the sake of other beings — and for this reason, at most, only the world-system itself, and not its beings, serves as the domain of their miraculous ability.

items.title: Section: Power Shared With Hearers and Solitary Buddhas — Closing the Five-Fold Classification

items.zh: 除上所說，所餘諸佛菩薩威力，當知麁相，與諸聲聞、獨覺等共。
items.en: Apart from what has already been described, the remaining power of buddhas and bodhisattvas should be understood as, at its coarser aspect, shared in common with hearers and solitary buddhas alike.

items.zh: 如是諸佛菩薩威力，聲聞、獨覺尚不能及，何況所餘一切天人異生外道。
items.en: Such power belonging to buddhas and bodhisattvas as this is beyond the reach even of hearers and solitary buddhas — how much more so beyond every other kind of god, human, ordinary being, or practitioner of a rival path.

items.title: Section: All Miraculous Display Reduces to Three — Body, Mind, and Speech — Closing the Chapter on Power Entirely

items.zh: 諸佛菩薩略有三種神變威力。一者、神境神變所攝，二者、記說神變所攝，三者、教誡神變所攝。
items.en: Buddhas and bodhisattvas possess, in brief, three kinds of miraculous transformative power: first, that comprised by the miraculous display of ability; second, that comprised by the miraculous display of discernment; and third, that comprised by the miraculous display of instruction.

items.zh: 當知此三，如其所應，攝入三種神通威力。謂神境智通威力、心差別智通威力、漏盡智通威力。
items.en: It should be understood that these three, as is fitting, are subsumed within three specific kinds of superknowledge power: the power of miraculous ability, the power of knowing minds, and the power of extinguishing contaminants.

blocks.text: The rest of the Buddha's innate power, then the chapter on power closes.

"In childhood, without any training, they are naturally skilful in every worldly craft. Without a teacher, alone in the great trichiliocosm, they attain unsurpassed awakening." Master Cháng Bǎi notes that the Buddha first studied with other teachers and found it was not enough. Then "Great Brahmā, lord of this world, comes down of his own accord, beseeching the Buddha to teach".
"Even should great thunderclouds roll in, they experience no disturbance."

"For six full years after awakening, Māra sought an opening and never found one." Master Cháng Bǎi: Māra kept watching for a moment of lapse. "Feeling, perception, and thought are known as they arise, abide, and cease." Sleeping "on the right side, like a lion", the Tathāgata "never shifts position".
"The great earth quakes, stars stream across the sky, every direction grows hot, heavenly music resounds." "All this is the Tathāgata's innate power, not produced by deliberate miracle."

"Every kind of power completely accomplished; every world and every realm of beings is its domain." A solitary buddha's domain is only the world, not its beings, "because a solitary buddha practises only to tame their own existence".
All display reduces to three: of ability (psychic power), of discernment (knowing minds), and of instruction (the extinction of contaminants, through which one teaches). Compare Day 237.

quiz.q: "Without a teacher … they attain unsurpassed awakening." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: finding austerity not ultimate, he left the ascetics' grove and awakened without a teacher
quiz.why: "Without a teacher, dwelling alone in the great trichiliocosm, they attain unsurpassed, perfect awakening." Master Cháng Bǎi: but he found it wasn't ultimate, left the forest of austerities, and awakened without a teacher.

quiz.q: The Buddha's concentration is undisturbed by thunder. In Master Cháng Bǎi's story of the woman in samādhi, who brought her out?
options: the Buddha summoned Bodhisattva Remover of Hindrances from below the earth — one snap and she emerged
quiz.why: "Their concentration is so utterly still that, even should great thunderclouds roll in, they experience no disturbance whatsoever." Master Cháng Bǎi: so the Buddha called Bodhisattva Remover of Hindrances up from beneath the earth; with one snap of his fingers, the woman emerged from samādhi.

quiz.q: "For six years Māra sought an opening and never found one." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: Māra kept seeking any sign of affliction or desire — and found none
quiz.why: "Having attained awakening, for six full years Māra sought any opening at all and never once found one." Master Cháng Bǎi: Māra kept looking for a chance — any sign of affliction or desire in the Buddha — but found none.

quiz.q: Of the three displays, "the display of discernment (記說)" — how do the masters explain it?
options: both: it's knowing others' minds — mental action
quiz.why: "First, that comprised by the miraculous display of ability; second, that comprised by the miraculous display of discernment; and third, that comprised by the miraculous display of instruction." Master Cháng Bǎi: 記 means discerning — able to tell others' inner thoughts; it's the transformation of knowing others' minds, included in mental action. Venerable Miào Jìng: the display of discernment is knowing others' minds — knowing beings' inner world.

quiz.q: Signs at final nirvāṇa "are innate power, not miraculous ability." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: an innate result of eons of the six perfections, not powers displayed in concentration
quiz.why: "All such immeasurable and truly extraordinary events as these are the Tathāgata's own innate power, not something produced by deliberately exercised miraculous ability." Master Cháng Bǎi: it's the inborn result of the Buddha's six perfections cultivated over eons — not something produced by powers displayed after entering concentration.

quiz.q: The solitary buddha "cultivates only to tame their own existence, not for beings." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: he never resolved to guide all beings — he lacks that compassion
quiz.why: "Because a solitary buddha cultivates their practice only to tame their own single existence, not for the sake of other beings." Venerable Miào Jìng: he didn't resolve to guide all beings — he doesn't have that compassion.
